units.text: EXT. BORDER CHECKPOINT - CONTINUOUS
Two TEENAGERS in a van queue take photographs of the fog on their phones, laughing.
A WAITER from the roadside cafe crosses the road carrying a tray of paper cups to the guards, steam curling off them.
Younger officer KESTREL OKONKWO, 20s, eager, jacket too clean, jogs over from the second booth.
Sir, the dog unit's flagged nothing on the left lane.
units.name: KESTREL

units.text: Good. Then we are all friends this morning.
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: He smiles at Delphine and slides her passport back through the slot.
Safe travels, Ms. Vass.
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: The barrier arm lifts.
The hatchback rolls forward ten feet, twenty.
Her shoulders drop.
Here is what I know about relief. It makes people careless with their hands.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: Her phone buzzes again against the dash.
She reaches for it without looking.
ON PHONE: did u get through?
She types with one thumb.
ON PHONE (CONT'D): yes. dont call me again
Halvorsen watches the hatchback in the mirror, thermos halfway to his lips.
Kestrel. The booster seat.
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: Sir?
units.name: KESTREL

units.text: Who rides to her sister's for three days with a child seat and no child?
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: Maybe the kid's with the sister already?
units.name: KESTREL

units.text: Then why is the seat belt buckled across it?
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: Silence.
The dog under the barrier lifts its head.
Close the arm.
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: Kestrel hits a button.
The barrier SLAMS down in front of the hatchback, fifteen feet from freedom.
Brake lights flare red in the fog.
Here is the thing nobody tells you. The calm is not the quiet part. The calm is the trap.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: Halvorsen walks out of the booth, unhurried, and Kestrel falls into step beside him.
They reach the driver's window together.
Ms. Vass. A moment.
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: Ma'am, please step out of the vehicle.
units.name: KESTREL

units.text: Please step out.
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: I have to be in Kalmar by noon. My sister is expecting me.
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: I have to be in Kalmar by noon.
units.name: ^DELPHINE

units.text: She does not move.
Her hands are tight on the wheel.
Not the baby-bird grip now.
Something harder.
There it is. Loose means practice. Tight means fear. Tight and then loose again, that means you have made up your mind.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: Delphine puts the car in reverse.
Halvorsen steps back.
Kestrel's hand drops to his belt.
Don't.
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: The engine revs.
Fog swallows the sound.
Somewhere beyond the barrier, a child begins to cry, thin and far away, from a truck in the other lane.
Delphine's eyes go wide.
She turns her head toward it.
That's not -
units.name: DELPHINE

units.text: The teenagers' phones all come up at once, filming.
Eleven years. I never once saw a border. Only the people standing very close to it.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: Ms. Vass. Whose child is in that truck?
units.name: HALVORSEN

units.text: She doesn't answer.
The engine cuts out.
The only sound is the dog, finally, barking.
